signature.name: Plaza Mayor de Lima
signature.detail: The historic heart of Lima and a UNESCO World Heritage site, lined with the Cathedral, Government Palace and Archbishop's Palace. Visit in the morning when the light is best and crowds are thinner; it's a short walk from the central bus and metro stops.

signature.name: Cathedral of Lima
signature.detail: A grand colonial cathedral holding the tomb of Francisco Pizarro and impressive religious art. Modest dress is recommended; entry is ticketed and includes the museum, so allow about an hour.

signature.name: Monastery of San Francisco
signature.detail: Famous for its catacombs and a library of ancient texts, this is one of Lima's most atmospheric religious sites. Guided tours run frequently; go early to avoid queues and bring a light jacket for the cool underground.

signature.name: Huaca Pucllana
signature.detail: A striking adobe pyramid from the Lima culture, right in the Miraflores district. Evening visits are especially scenic with the site illuminated; book a guided tour in advance as access is by tour only.

signature.name: Pachacamac
signature.detail: A vast archaeological complex of temples and pyramids south of the city, once a major pilgrimage center. It's best visited in the morning; bring sun protection and water as the site is exposed and large.

transport: Metro $0.40 a ride; taxis $3-6 for short trips
